Northwind emailed Marco on Sunday night to report that their invoices had exported with the wrong tax rate for their Dutch entity, and their finance team only caught it after some had already been sent to clients [[M1#16]]. Diego traced it to the rounding change from August, which only affected accounts with multiple tax jurisdictions — essentially just Northwind [[M1#17]]. Forty-one invoices over two weeks were affected [[M1#19]].

The fix and follow-up:
- Diego fixed the calculation the same day and sent Northwind a note listing the affected invoice numbers by the next morning so they could issue corrections; regenerating the already-sent PDFs was the awkward part [[M1#19]][[M1#20]][[M1#21]].
- Marco called their CFO himself and told Diego not to promise any credit in the note until after that call [[M1#20]][[M1#23]].

At the September 29 retro, Diego cited Northwind as something that went well — a bad week, fixed in a day, and the customer stayed [[M4#2]].

The biggest drop-off is at the billing address step in checkout. With two additional weeks of data as of the September 15 sync, Sofía measured a 29% drop at that step, flat across plans and countries [[M2#1]]. A week earlier, the early data showed 28% of people who picked a plan leaving on that screen [[M3#11]].

Sofía's recommendation was to remove the address step for card payments and keep it for bank transfer and invoice-based plans, since Stripe validates the postcode itself [[M2#1]]; Marco approved it, with Diego and Ana building it and shipping one week after the pricing page, around October 22 [[M2#6]][[M2#7]].
